text: CHAPTER 34
speaker: Narrator

text: The Woman He Chose
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The corridor was a lung.
speaker: Narrator

text: It contracted and expanded around them with a slow, rhythmic wheeze of stone. Dust drifted from the ceiling in thin gray threads, caught and released with each breath the passage took. The oily stone sweated moisture that smelled of copper and wet earth, and beneath that something colder—the smell of anything in this place that had decided to remember them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik walked with one hand resting on his satchel.
speaker: Narrator

text: The journal no longer felt like a book. It felt like a hook set somewhere behind his ribs, its weight tugging with every step. Every step reminded him of the price he had paid to keep Ninsun real. Every step also reminded him that the reason for that price was gone.
speaker: Narrator

text: He had always believed that understanding a price preserved some ownership over the transaction. He had traded sleep for profit, honesty for the Collector's coin, comfort for survival. The City had shown him the flaw in that belief. It took the receipt along with the goods.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind him, Ninsun kept pace.
speaker: Narrator

text: Her footsteps were light against the stone. For the first hour after the corridor swallowed the previous chamber he had kept expecting them to disappear—for the rhythm behind him simply to stop, the way a heartbeat stops, without announcement. He kept expecting her shape to blur, her name to slip through his fingers the way water slips through a cracked jar.
speaker: Narrator

text: She was still there.
speaker: Narrator

text: He knew her name–Ninsun. Nothing followed the name.
speaker: Narrator

text: He could remember the payment.
speaker: Narrator

text: He no longer remembered why.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag walked ahead, axe resting across his shoulders, the pack heavy on his back. Whatever had knocked from inside it had remained quiet since the fourth strike. He had not opened the straps. Curiosity, they had learned, was often a form of consent.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu kept to the side, the golden figurine still in her possession. She simply carried it, as though carrying it had become part of a route whose purpose belonged to someone else.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor narrowed without warning.
speaker: Narrator

text: The walls pressed close enough that Zik's shoulders brushed both sides. Looking back had begun to feel like asking a question the City might answer with a cost. He did not look back.
speaker: Narrator

text: After a time the walls eased. The corridor opened into a wider section scored with shallow parallel grooves, as though something large had been dragged through it more than once. The air grew colder. The copper smell thickened.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun spoke for the first time since they had left the ledger chamber.
speaker: Narrator

text: You don't remember why.
speaker: Ninsun

text: It was not a question.
speaker: Narrator

text: No.
speaker: Zik

text: But you remember that you chose.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Yes.
speaker: Zik

text: A longer silence. Then:
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Does that still count?
speaker: Ninsun

text: He did not answer immediately. Some questions were themselves transactions.
speaker: Narrator

text: It counts to me,
speaker: Zik

text: he said at last.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: He was not sure whether that was true.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun did not press. She walked a few paces farther and then said, almost to herself,
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The tablets never mentioned this part. The part where you keep the person and lose the reason.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag glanced back once.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You two finished? The floor ahead looks wrong.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik tested it out of habit. His body still knew the sequence even if the conscious lesson was gone. The stone held. They continued.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor began to slope more steeply. At one point the torch caught a pale scar in the limestone—the ghost of a name crossed out so thoroughly only the shape of the erasure remained. He did not stop to read it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind him Ninsun's breathing stayed steady. He counted it without meaning to: the quiet intake, the quieter release. As long as he could hear it, the payment was still holding.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not know how long payments held in this place.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not know whether the City considered the transaction closed or merely deferred.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor turned.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ahead the stone opened into a chamber whose far wall was lost in shadow. The air moved differently here—not the breathing of the passage, but a slow circulation that seemed to come from below the floor itself. Four shallow depressions marked the threshold, each the size of a kneeling figure. A fifth depression sat slightly apart, empty and darker than the rest.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag stopped.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: This is new.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu tilted her head, studying the darkness.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Or very old.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Ninsun came up beside Zik. She did not touch him. She simply stood close enough that he could feel the fact of her presence without needing the memory of its value.
speaker: Narrator

text: You chose me,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said quietly. Not accusing. Not grateful. Stating the remaining fact.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I did.
speaker: Zik
